source_authority: The supplied image is the exact identity authority: the September 1993 premiere issue of VIBE magazine — the black-and-white Snoop Doggy Dogg cover with the large cropped VIBE masthead and the magenta BOW WOW WOW cover line — lying flat on a dark charcoal surface. Every element of the cover art, its typography, its photograph, and the framing of the magazine on the surface must look exactly as captured whenever the cover is visible, and the magazine must return to exactly this captured state at the end.
style_lock: the cover photograph, masthead, and cover lines are never redrawn, retouched, recolored, sharpened, or modernized; the slightly worn 1993 print scan character is the identity
the magazine keeps its exact printed proportions; it never changes size, position on the surface, or perspective while closed
the pages glimpsed during the riffle look like genuine early-1990s editorial print: dense serif text columns, black-and-white photography, bold display headlines — consistent with this exact issue
paper behaves like real coated magazine stock throughout: thin flexible sheets that bow under tension and release crisply
the dark charcoal surface under the magazine stays perfectly still and empty for the entire clip
motion: The magazine performs one fast thumb-riffle, the way a person fans through a print magazine to sample it. Beat 1: the closed magazine holds exactly as captured. Beat 2: the front cover and the block of pages beneath it bow upward slightly from the right edge, held under tension as a gently curved stack. Beat 3: the pages release in a rapid cascade from front to back — a quick continuous flutter in which many individual sheets flash past in well under two seconds, each briefly glimpsed page carrying believable editorial print texture: text columns, black-and-white photographs, headline typography racing by too fast to read but unmistakably this magazine's design language. The cascade runs smoothly right to left, sheet after sheet, with natural accelerating rhythm like a released spring. Beat 4: the last sheet settles, the block flattens, and the closed magazine lies exactly as captured again. Beat 5: the closed magazine holds identical to the first frame through to the end. The magazine body never slides or rotates during the riffle; only the sheets move.
timing: Hold the exact captured cover for the opening moment, spend a short beat on the tensioned bow, let the cascade itself run fast — a blur of successive sheets — then settle cleanly, and hold the closed magazine exactly as captured for the entire final stretch so the last frame is identical to the first.
camera: Static camera, directly above-front of the magazine at the captured angle. No zoom, no pan, no rotation, no dolly, no perspective change, no depth-of-field shift, no lighting change.
background: The dark charcoal surface exactly as captured: uniform, still, no texture change, no shadows appearing or disappearing beyond the natural soft flicker of moving pages, nothing else ever enters the frame.
negative_constraints: no hands, fingers, or any person visible; the riffle happens as if thumbed but no one is shown
no added objects, text overlays, logos, watermarks, or reflections
the cover must never be redrawn or reinterpreted when it returns; final frame identical to the first
